Header: Oxalis latifolia ( Oxalis corniculata , Oxalis radicosa ) Ubwunyu bwa nyamanza in Kinyarwanda language, Oseille or trèfle in French language

Prevention: Oxalis – weed problems are known from the area and are severe.
Avoid intensive cultivation of other crops in coffee plantations as harvest of other crops allows
Oxalis to thrive, and its bulbs are spread.
Mow repeatedly many times as the
Monitoring: Look for small plants without short stem but with 14-45 leaves.
Each leaf is composed of 3 fishtail- shaped leaflets linked to each other.
The bulb in the soil looks like a small whitish carrot (diameter: 1-2 cm)
Oxalis is only a problematic weed when occurring in masses and only in young coffee plantations.
Direct Control: Oxalis leaves can be freshly eaten as salads, but only if coffee, other crops, or weeds around
Oxalis were not treated with chemicals.
Deep tillage to expose bulbs to drought
